reason: The text repeatedly portrays Yahweh in a supportive and favor-granting relationship with Joseph, who is explicitly identified as Hebrew ('אִישׁ עִבְרִי'). Key phrases demonstrate consistent divine favor: 'וַיְהִ֤י יְהוָה֙ אֶת־יוֹסֵ֔ף' (Yahweh was WITH Joseph) appears multiple times, emphasizing divine presence. Joseph is described as 'אִ֣ישׁ מַצְלִ֑יחַ' (a prosperous/successful man) because Yahweh made all his endeavors prosper ('יְהוָ֖ה מַצְלִ֥יחַ בְּיָדֽוֹ'). Yahweh even extended blessing to the Egyptian master's household specifically because of Joseph ('וַיְבָ֧רֶךְ יְהוָ֛ה אֶת־ בֵּ֥ית הַמִּצְרִ֖י בִּגְלַ֣ל יוֹסֵ֑ף'). Even during his imprisonment following false accusation, Yahweh continued to show Joseph favor, kindness ('חָ֑סֶד'), and grace ('חִנּ֔וֹ'). This narrative demonstrates divine protection and support toward a Hebrew, not antagonism.
